chunks: Saad narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubayd Allah al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you have prayed a prayer while you are in the mosque and the prayer is established, if you wish, you may leave, and if you wish, pray with them, and make it a tasbih (supplication/praise)."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one has already prayed before the congregational prayer starts?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the flexibility of congregational prayer, allowing those who have already prayed to join the community either by repeating the prayer or by having their previous act counted as voluntary praise (Tasbih). This reflects the Shia emphasis on the spiritual value of communal unity (Jama'ah) while accommodating individual circumstances, as recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*. The permissibility of treating a completed obligatory prayer as a supererogatory act underscores the fluidity between fard and nafl in certain contexts of mosque etiquette.
